Use the image_gen tool to generate exactly one image, then reply with the saved file path only. Do not write code or run commands.
Use case: illustration-story. The attached image is a STYLE reference only: match its vintage Polish educational field-guide drawing, precise dark pen contours, fine restrained crosshatching and flat hand-tinted colour. Do not copy the man.
Asset: one text-free specimen illustration for an Andrzejki wax-pouring reading. Draw a single solid wax cast, the kind formed when hot candle wax is poured through the hole of an old key into a bowl of cold water and sets at once. Mostly pale ivory wax (#f4f0e7) warming to honey-ochre (#d49a2a) in the thick parts. A chunky, connected mass with crinkled lobes, flat splashed fans, knobbly bubbles, small holes and a few thin dripping tendrils; ink contours and restrained hatching for volume. It must look like a genuine accidental wax cast, organic and irregular, never a carved sculpture, a toy or a clean outline. Its overall outline, read as a shadow on a wall, loosely suggests the subject below, the way a cloud resembles something: recognisable after a moment, still accidental.
Composition: the cast alone, centred, seen from the side as if held up to a candle, whole cast visible with 8% clear margin, square canvas. Actual transparent background. No bowl, water, candle, key, hand, ground, cast shadow, paper texture, frame, labels, letters, numbers, logos or watermark. No photorealism, no 3D render.
